head: 7bcf48ac0ca61b029ca119d8869b71636ffaef72
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (independent reviewer for the F16 delivery session)
scope: The full diff of main..f16-dispatch-brief at 7bcf48ac0 and the design change on engineering; probed briefs in headings, chains, included targets, nested directives and dispatches in briefs, sets, picks, -c mode and the eval's premature_dispatch rule.
criteria: AC1-AC9 and AC11 against the fixtures, unit tests, docs and eval tests.
validation: make check exit 0 (2257 tests, harness 1089, corpus 650 of 650); make eval-harness 849 passed.

findings.description: A briefed dispatch written in a heading crashed with E_UNEXPECTED_INTERNAL_ERROR: the heading's slug kept the mark the lifted link drops.
A malformed brief fragment such as #given%zz crashed with E_UNEXPECTED_INTERNAL_ERROR instead of E_INVALID_CONVERSION_METADATA.
The dispatch line landed under the brief's last child heading or composed destination, and in a set later members' lines did too.
A brief's own dispatch lines in a set read as extra set members.
Briefs dispatching each other reported E_HEADING_DEPTH_OVERFLOW instead of E_DISPATCH_CYCLE.
New diagnostics lacked location or chain, or described a dispatch as a directive.
docs/dispatch.md overclaimed when briefed dispatches share a sub-section.
Docs and docstrings were stale on level-6 overflow and generated structure.
A brief copied twice carried its nested dispatch sub-sections only in its first copy.

findings.description: A brief nested two deep shared one placing across its copies, so copies pointed into each other.
A brief merged parallel links from different sections into one set.
A brief cycle starting deep reported E_HEADING_DEPTH_OVERFLOW.

A brief composing the section dispatching it was reported as a composition cycle naming a directive.
